ui_bugs.issue: Playwright could not observe dash_0/1/2 frames cycling on the local user's avatar during a far-click move. Avatar position updates correctly (>260px stage distance), but only idle_0/1/2 frames render in across a 3.5s sample window (50ms granularity). useChatSocket case 'move' resets anim_stance to 'idle' (lib/useChatSocket.js L113); ChatWindow.handleMove sends move FIRST then stance:dash (ChatWindow.jsx L157-158), so the order should net to dash, but client never observes it. Either WS broadcast ordering is being violated, or stance:dash is not being sent/processed. Main agent reports self-test confirmed dash works — needs human/manual verification.

action_items: Verify ghost dash anim manually: pick ghost via Sprites picker, click far in iso-world, and visually confirm dash_0/1/2 frames cycle on YOUR avatar (not via screenshot — by eye over ~1.3s). Current order works in theory but is fragile.

rca of the issue: Ghost dash inconclusive: ChatWindow.handleMove at L157 sends 'move' before 'stance:dash' at L158. useChatSocket case 'move' (L113 of lib/useChatSocket.js) resets anim_stance to 'idle' on every move broadcast for ANY user including self. So if both messages broadcast in order, client should land on 'dash'. If they're out of order (rare but possible), client lands on 'idle'. Playwright observation showed only idle frames over 3.5s. Either the stance broadcast isn't reaching the client, OR a setTimeout-based stance:idle is firing too early. Recommend swapping send order in handleMove (stance first, move second) for robustness.
